To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

female rats bred for high running capacity have lower body weight and fat mass and increased running capacity, compared to female rats bred for low running capacity, and that the high running capacity female rats have lower body weight, fat mass, and running capacity, compared with male rats.
female low runners (LRF) have a lower body weight, higher fat mass, and lower lean mass than female high runners (HRF).
rats bred for high running capacity (HRC) have lower body fat, lower body mass, and higher lean mass than rats bred for low running capacity (LRC).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of physical activity on the peripheral nervous system and its relevance to pain.
the role of exercise and diet on the nervous system.
the role of diet and exercise in the prevention and treatment of pain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
female rats bred for high running capacity display differences in the periphery that may be relevant to neuropathy.
rats bred for low and/or high voluntary wheel running capacity display differences in metabolic and pain relevant peripheral tissues and nerves.
female rats bred for low and/or high running capacity display differences in peripheral nerves and pain-related behaviors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
rats bred for low (LRC) and high (HRC) running capacity differ in peripheral nerve and muscle function.
rats bred for high voluntary running capacity (HRC) are more resistant to neuropathy than rats bred for low voluntary running capacity (LRC).
rats with low running capacity (LRC) have a higher metabolic rate, more oxidative stress, and greater pain sensitivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rats bred for high activity display a more favorable metabolic profile and nerve health than those bred for low activity.
female rats with high running capacity have lower levels of neuropathy and pain than female rats with low running capacity.
female rats with high running capacity have lower levels of circulating triglycerides, lower body weight, higher levels of insulin, and lower body temperature than rats with lower capacity.
